title: Anand Vihar Metro to Anand Vihar Namo Bharat RRTS Station: Complete Walking Route Guide
description: Step by step guide to walk from Anand Vihar Metro Blue Line to the Namo Bharat RRTS station. Platform directions, exit route, and FAQs included.
body:
If you are traveling on the Delhi Metro Pink Line/Blue Line and need to switch to the Namo Bharat RRTS at Anand Vihar, the transfer is simple once you know the exact platform and exit to look for. Many first time travelers end up walking in circles because the signage inside the station is not always easy to spot in a hurry. This guide breaks down the entire route step by step, based on an actual visit to the station, so you can make the switch quickly and without confusion.

Anand Vihar is one of the most important interchange points in the National Capital Region. It connects the Delhi Metro Blue Line, the Pink Line, the Anand Vihar Railway Terminal, the Anand Vihar ISBT, and now the Namo Bharat RRTS corridor that runs between Sarai Kale Khan and Meerut. Since so many transport systems meet at one place, knowing the shortest walking path can save a lot of time, especially during rush hour.

## Understanding the Platforms at Anand Vihar

The Blue Line at Anand Vihar runs between Dwarka Sector 21 on one end and Vaishali on the other. Trains in each direction use separate platforms, and the platform you land on depends on which direction you are traveling from.

**Platform 4** is used when your train is coming from the Shiv Vihar side towards Anand Vihar. If you are standing on Platform 3 and need to reach Platform 4, you need to take the stairs. 

**Platform 3** is used for trains heading from Anand Vihar towards Shiv Vihar. If you are on Platform 4 and need to reach Platform 3, you need to take the stairs. 

**Platform 2** takes you toward Dwarka Sector 21 from Anand Vihar. 

**Platform 1** takes you to the final station of the Blue Line on the Anand Vihar side, which is Vaishali. 

Knowing whether you are in the front or back section of your metro coach makes a real difference here, since it decides whether turning left or right gets you to the correct platform faster.

## Finding the Exit Towards the RRTS Station

Once you are on the platform, head towards Platform 1. As you walk along the platform, look for the staircase area. Right next to the platform 1 stairs, you will see the exit sign. This is the exit you need to take to reach the Namo Bharat station, so do not exit from another exit gates unless you have already spotted this exit point.

If you are on the pink line, then you have to follow these steps;

- **If arriving from Shiv Vihar (Welcome, Krishna Nagar, Maujpur) towards Anand Vihar, in front of the train:** Exit Platform 4 and turn **right** and if you are at the back of the train, then turn **left.** 
- **If arriving from Majlis Park (Delhi Cantt, Netaji Subhash Place, Shalimar Bagh, Lajpat Nagar, Sarojini Nagar) towards Anand Vihar (front of train):** Exit Platform 3 and turn **left** but if you are at the back of the train, then take the stairs and turn **right.** 
- **If you are at the centre or have taken the lift, then just walk straight towards Platform 1.**

Next, head toward Platform 1; the exit is located right next to the stairs.

## Step by Step Walking Directions After the Exit

After you take the exit, the path to the Namo Bharat RRTS station goes like this:

1. Take the exit and turn left.
2. Walk straight and you will see a direction board in front of you.
3. After the board, turn right.
4. Continue walking and then turn left. Here you will spot the board for the Anand Vihar Namo Bharat RRTS station.

This route involves a left, then a right, then a final left. It sounds like a lot of turns on paper, but in person the signage at each point makes it easy to follow once you know the sequence in advance.

## Why This Route Matters for Commuters

Anand Vihar connects three major transport hubs within walking distance of each other. Someone arriving from Ghaziabad or Vaishali on the Blue Line, heading to catch a Namo Bharat train towards Sahibabad, Duhai, Modinagar, or further up to Meerut, benefits directly from knowing this shortcut. Instead of wasting time asking for directions or backtracking after taking a wrong exit, you can walk straight to the RRTS entry gates.

This is also useful for people heading the other way, arriving on the Namo Bharat RRTS from Meerut or Ghaziabad and wanting to catch a Blue Line train onward to Vaishali, Dwarka, or anywhere in between.

## Tips for a Smooth Transfer

- Keep your metro card or QR ticket ready in one pocket and your RRTS ticket or card in another, so you are not fumbling at the gates.
- If you are traveling during peak hours, the platforms and connecting corridors can get crowded, so stay alert for the direction boards rather than following the crowd, since not everyone around you may be headed to the same exit.
- The walk between the Blue Line platform and the Namo Bharat station takes a few minutes on foot, so plan a small buffer if you have a train to catch.
- Since both Delhi Metro and Namo Bharat use separate ticketing systems, remember you will need a valid RRTS ticket or card separately. Your metro ticket will not work at the RRTS gates.

## Final Thoughts

The transfer between Anand Vihar Metro and the Anand Vihar Namo Bharat RRTS station is straightforward once you know the exact sequence of turns. Right or left at the platform depending on your direction, then left, board, right, and left again after the exit. Keep this sequence in mind, watch for the direction boards along the way, and you will reach the RRTS gates without any trouble, even during your first visit.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### **Is Anand Vihar Namo Bharat station connected directly to the metro station?** 

Yes, the Namo Bharat RRTS station at Anand Vihar is linked to the Delhi Metro Blue Line station through a short walking path with a common exit, so passengers can transfer between the two without leaving the overall station complex.

### **Do I need a separate ticket for the Namo Bharat RRTS train?** 

Yes. The Namo Bharat RRTS runs on its own ticketing system, separate from Delhi Metro. You will need to buy a fresh ticket or use an RRTS card at the RRTS gates, even if you already have a Delhi Metro ticket or card.

### **How long does it take to walk from the Blue Line platform to the RRTS station?** 

On average, the walk takes about five to seven minutes, depending on how crowded the station is and how quickly you locate the correct exit and turns.

### **Which platform should I use if I am coming from Vaishali?** 

If you are arriving from the Vaishali side, you will land on Platform 2. From there, follow signs towards Platform 1 to find the exit leading to the RRTS station.

### **What if I take the wrong exit at Anand Vihar?** 

If you take a wrong exit, you may end up near the ISBT or the railway terminal side instead of the RRTS entrance. In that case, the easiest fix is to go back inside the metro station and follow the platform 1 exit route described above.

### **Does this route apply to both directions, towards Meerut and towards Sarai Kale Khan?** 

Yes. Once you reach the Namo Bharat RRTS station at Anand Vihar, you can catch trains in either direction, towards Sarai Kale Khan on one side or towards Sahibabad, Duhai, Modinagar, and Meerut on the other, from the same station.

### **Is there a lift or escalator available on this route?** 

Most Delhi Metro interchange stations, including Anand Vihar, have escalators and lifts near the main staircases. Availability at each specific turn can vary, so if you are traveling with luggage or need step free access, it helps to ask station staff at the entry gate for the nearest lift.
